questions.question: What’s our most popular payment method?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    payment_type,
    COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS orders_paid,
    round(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT order_id)
          / (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) FROM order_payments), 2) AS pct_of_orders
FROM order_payments
GROUP BY payment_type
ORDER BY orders_paid DESC
LIMIT 1
questions.note: I measured popularity as the number of distinct orders that used each payment method, across all order statuses. Because some orders are split across several methods, the percentages can add up to more than 100%.

questions.question: Which 5 product categories brought in the most revenue in 2017?
questions.sql:
SELECT coalesce(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category,
       round(sum(oi.price), 2) AS revenue
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
LEFT JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01'
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-01-01'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY revenue DESC
LIMIT 5
questions.note: Revenue is item sales (sum of unit price, excluding freight), since the breakdown is by category, and canceled and unavailable orders are excluded.

questions.question: Who are our top 10 sellers by number of orders, and what are their average review scores?
questions.sql:
WITH seller_orders AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT seller_id, order_id
  FROM order_items
),
seller_counts AS (
  SELECT seller_id, count(*) AS order_count
  FROM seller_orders
  GROUP BY seller_id
),
seller_scores AS (
  SELECT so.seller_id, avg(r.review_score) AS avg_score
  FROM seller_orders so
  JOIN order_reviews r ON r.order_id = so.order_id
  GROUP BY so.seller_id
)
SELECT sc.seller_id,
       sc.order_count,
       round(ss.avg_score, 2) AS avg_review_score
FROM seller_counts sc
LEFT JOIN seller_scores ss ON ss.seller_id = sc.seller_id
ORDER BY sc.order_count DESC, sc.seller_id
LIMIT 10
questions.note: I counted an order for a seller if it contains at least one of that seller's items, and included all order statuses since the question doesn't mention sales or revenue. Review averages use the review rows for those orders, and sellers with no reviews show NULL.

questions.question: How long does it take on average from purchase to delivery, by state?
questions.sql:
SELECT c.customer_state AS state,
       round(avg(extract(epoch FROM o.order_delivered_customer_date - o.order_purchase_timestamp) / 86400)::numeric, 2) AS avg_delivery_days
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
  AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY c.customer_state
ORDER BY avg_delivery_days DESC
questions.note: I used the customer's state (`customers.customer_state`) since the question concerns where orders are delivered, and restricted to delivered orders with a delivery date, per the delivery-time rule.

questions.question: Do customers who pay in more installments spend more per order?
questions.sql:
WITH order_pay AS (
  SELECT order_id,
         SUM(payment_value) AS paid,
         MAX(payment_installments) FILTER (WHERE payment_installments >= 1) AS max_inst
  FROM order_payments
  GROUP BY order_id
),
sales AS (
  SELECT o.order_id, p.paid, p.max_inst
  FROM orders o
  JOIN order_pay p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
  WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
    AND p.max_inst IS NOT NULL
),
bucketed AS (
  SELECT order_id, paid, max_inst,
         CASE WHEN max_inst = 1 THEN '1 (paid at once)'
              WHEN max_inst <= 3 THEN '2-3'
              WHEN max_inst <= 6 THEN '4-6'
              WHEN max_inst <= 10 THEN '7-10'
              ELSE '11+'
         END AS installment_bucket,
         CASE WHEN max_inst = 1 THEN 1
              WHEN max_inst <= 3 THEN 2
              WHEN max_inst <= 6 THEN 3
              WHEN max_inst <= 10 THEN 4
              ELSE 5
         END AS sort_key
  FROM sales
)
SELECT installment_bucket,
       COUNT(*) AS orders,
       ROUND(AVG(paid), 2) AS avg_spend_per_order
FROM bucketed
GROUP BY installment_bucket, sort_key
ORDER BY sort_key
questions.note: I measured spend per order as total payments (`payment_value`, including freight and any card interest), using each order's highest installment count. Canceled and unavailable orders are excluded. Orders with an installment count of 0 are ignored when picking that maximum.

questions.question: Which product categories get the most 1-star reviews as a share of their orders?
questions.sql:
WITH order_categories AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT oi.order_id,
         coalesce(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category
  FROM order_items oi
  JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
),
one_star_orders AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT order_id
  FROM order_reviews
  WHERE review_score = 1
)
SELECT oc.category,
       count(*) AS orders,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE os.order_id IS NOT NULL) AS one_star_orders,
       round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE os.order_id IS NOT NULL) / count(*), 2) AS one_star_share_pct
FROM order_categories oc
LEFT JOIN one_star_orders os ON os.order_id = oc.order_id
GROUP BY oc.category
ORDER BY one_star_share_pct DESC
questions.note: I counted each order once per category, using all order statuses in the denominator. An order counts as one-star if it has at least one review with score 1. Orders with no review therefore count as not one-star, so categories with many undelivered orders will look lower. Small categories can show extreme shares, so check the order counts before drawing conclusions.

questions.question: How did monthly revenue trend in 2018 compared to the same months in 2017?
questions.sql:
WITH monthly AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', o.order_purchase_timestamp)::date AS month_start,
         sum(p.payment_value) AS revenue
  FROM orders o
  JOIN order_payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
  WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
    AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01'
    AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-09-01'
  GROUP BY 1
),
pivoted AS (
  SELECT extract(month FROM month_start)::int AS month_num,
         sum(CASE WHEN extract(year FROM month_start) = 2017 THEN revenue END) AS rev_2017,
         sum(CASE WHEN extract(year FROM month_start) = 2018 THEN revenue END) AS rev_2018
  FROM monthly
  WHERE extract(month FROM month_start) <= 8
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT month_num,
       round(rev_2017, 2) AS revenue_2017,
       round(rev_2018, 2) AS revenue_2018,
       round(100.0 * (rev_2018 - rev_2017) / nullif(rev_2017, 0), 2) AS yoy_growth_pct
FROM pivoted
ORDER BY month_num
questions.note: Revenue is taken as payment value (excluding canceled and unavailable orders), and the comparison covers January to August, since 2018-09 and later are incomplete in the data.

questions.question: Are late deliveries hurting our review scores? Compare on-time vs. late orders.
questions.reason: no predicted column matches gold column 'late'
questions.sql:
WITH delivered AS (
  SELECT order_id,
         CASE WHEN order_delivered_customer_date > order_estimated_delivery_date
              THEN 'late' ELSE 'on time' END AS delivery_status
  FROM orders
  WHERE order_status = 'delivered' AND order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
),
reviews_once AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT d.delivery_status, r.review_id, r.review_score
  FROM delivered d
  JOIN order_reviews r ON r.order_id = d.order_id
)
SELECT delivery_status,
       count(*) AS review_count,
       round(avg(review_score), 2) AS avg_review_score,
       round(100.0 * avg(CASE WHEN review_score <= 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 2) AS low_score_pct
FROM reviews_once
GROUP BY delivery_status
ORDER BY delivery_status
questions.note: I compared delivered orders with a delivery date, splitting them into late (delivered after the estimated date) and on time, and counted each review_id once per delivery group. Low scores are defined as 1 or 2 stars. This shows association only, not proof that lateness causes lower scores.

questions.question: For each of the top 3 categories by revenue, which month in 2018 was their best?
questions.sql:
WITH cat_rev AS (
  SELECT coalesce(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category,
         sum(oi.price) AS revenue
  FROM order_items oi
  JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
  JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
  WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
  GROUP BY 1
),
top3 AS (
  SELECT category, revenue
  FROM cat_rev
  ORDER BY revenue DESC
  LIMIT 3
),
monthly AS (
  SELECT coalesce(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category,
         date_trunc('month', o.order_purchase_timestamp)::date AS month,
         sum(oi.price) AS revenue
  FROM order_items oi
  JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
  JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
  WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
    AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-01-01'
    AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-09-01'
  GROUP BY 1, 2
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT m.category,
         m.month,
         m.revenue,
         t.revenue AS total_revenue,
         rank() OVER (PARTITION BY m.category ORDER BY m.revenue DESC) AS rk
  FROM monthly m
  JOIN top3 t ON t.category = m.category
)
SELECT category,
       month AS best_month_2018,
       round(revenue, 2) AS best_month_revenue,
       round(total_revenue, 2) AS total_revenue_all_periods
FROM ranked
WHERE rk = 1
ORDER BY total_revenue DESC
questions.note: Assumptions: "top 3" is ranked on item sales (SUM of `price`, excluding canceled and unavailable orders) across all periods. The best month is searched only within Jan to Aug 2018, because Sep and Oct 2018 are incomplete in the data.

questions.question: Which sellers had sales increase every quarter in 2018?
questions.sql:
WITH seller_quarters AS (
  SELECT oi.seller_id,
         CASE
           WHEN o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-01-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-04-01' THEN 1
           WHEN o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-04-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-07-01' THEN 2
           WHEN o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-07-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-09-01' THEN 3
         END AS quarter_no,
         oi.price
  FROM order_items oi
  JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
  WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
    AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-01-01'
    AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-09-01'
),
quarterly_sales AS (
  SELECT seller_id, quarter_no, sum(price) AS sales
  FROM seller_quarters
  WHERE quarter_no IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY seller_id, quarter_no
),
pivoted AS (
  SELECT seller_id,
         max(CASE WHEN quarter_no = 1 THEN sales END) AS q1_sales,
         max(CASE WHEN quarter_no = 2 THEN sales END) AS q2_sales,
         max(CASE WHEN quarter_no = 3 THEN sales END) AS q3_sales
  FROM quarterly_sales
  GROUP BY seller_id
)
SELECT seller_id,
       round(q1_sales, 2) AS q1_2018_sales,
       round(q2_sales, 2) AS q2_2018_sales,
       round(q3_sales, 2) AS q3_2018_sales
FROM pivoted
WHERE q1_sales IS NOT NULL
  AND q2_sales IS NOT NULL
  AND q3_sales IS NOT NULL
  AND q2_sales > q1_sales
  AND q3_sales > q2_sales
ORDER BY seller_id

  GROUP BY seller_id
)
SELECT seller_id,
       round(q1_sales, 2) AS q1_2018_sales,
       round(q2_sales, 2) AS q2_2018_sales,
       round(q3_2018_sales_placeholder, 2) AS q3_2018_sales
FROM pivoted
WHERE q1_sales IS NOT NULL
  AND q2_sales IS NOT NULL
  AND q3_sales IS NOT NULL
  AND q2_sales > q1_sales
  AND q3_sales > q2_sales
ORDER BY seller_id

WITH seller_quarters AS (
  SELECT oi.seller_id,
         CASE
           WHEN o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-01-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-04-01' THEN 1
           WHEN o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-04-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-07-01' THEN 2
           WHEN o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-07-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-09-01' THEN 3
         END AS quarter_no,
         oi.price
  FROM order_items oi
  JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
  WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
    AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-01-01'
    AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-09-01'
),
quarterly_sales AS (
  SELECT seller_id, quarter_no, sum(price) AS sales
  FROM seller_quarters
  WHERE quarter_no IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY seller_id, quarter_no
),
pivoted AS (
  SELECT seller_id,
         max(CASE WHEN quarter_no = 1 THEN sales END) AS q1_sales,
         max(CASE WHEN quarter_no = 2 THEN sales END) AS q2_sales,
         max(CASE WHEN quarter_no = 3 THEN sales END) AS q3_sales
  FROM quarterly_sales
  GROUP BY seller_id
)
SELECT seller_id,
       round(q1_sales, 2) AS q1_2018_sales,
       round(q2_sales, 2) AS q2_2018_sales,
       round(q3_sales, 2) AS q3_2018_sales
FROM pivoted
WHERE q1_sales IS NOT NULL
  AND q2_sales IS NOT NULL
  AND q3_sales IS NOT NULL
  AND q2_sales > q1_sales
  AND q3_sales > q2_sales
ORDER BY seller_id

questions.question: What’s the average time between a repeat customer’s first and second order?
questions.sql:
WITH ordered AS (
  SELECT c.customer_unique_id,
         o.order_purchase_timestamp AS purchased_at,
         row_number() OVER (
           PARTITION BY c.customer_unique_id
           ORDER BY o.order_purchase_timestamp, o.order_id
         ) AS n
  FROM orders o
  JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
), first_two AS (
  SELECT customer_unique_id,
         max(purchased_at) FILTER (WHERE n = 1) AS first_order_at,
         max(purchased_at) FILTER (WHERE n = 2) AS second_order_at
  FROM ordered
  WHERE n <= 2
  GROUP BY customer_unique_id
  HAVING count(*) = 2
)
SELECT round(avg(extract(epoch FROM second_order_at - first_order_at) / 86400)::numeric, 2) AS avg_days_first_to_second
FROM first_two
questions.note: I counted a repeat customer as a unique person (`customer_unique_id`) with at least two orders, and included all order statuses since this is a timing question, not a revenue one. The result is the mean gap in days, as a decimal.
